projects.title: LARA
projects.subtitle: Exploring the mechanics of motion.
projects.summary: A robotic arm study connecting mechanical design, inverse kinematics, simulation, and visual joint tracking.
notes: The repository contains multiple mechanical revisions and a legacy MuJoCo model with an inverse-kinematics heart-trace demonstration.
A separate AprilTag generator produces twelve markers for six joints. Visual pose tracking requires measured marker-to-link transforms.
Tool changing and surface-finishing ideas appear in planning notes; they are proposed demonstrations rather than verified physical capabilities.

projects.title: Pop-up Spoiler
projects.subtitle: Two ESP32 boards translate adjustable roll and pitch response curves into coordinated motion for four encoder-feedback motors.
projects.summary: A pop-up spoiler prototype for a third-generation BMW 6 Series. Four feedback-controlled motors move two wings through four-bar linkages, with adjustable response curves for sensed roll and pitch.
notes: Four bars, one guided motion: each wing rides on connected arms that lift and tilt it along a defined path, rather than simply turning around a hinge.

Getting the dimensions right: arm lengths and pivot spacing must produce the required lift, tilt, and clearance together. Near the flat starting position, small errors or joint play can make the linkage bind or move unpredictably.

Two motors per wing: powering both arms is intended to share the load. The unequal arms need different, coordinated angles; encoder feedback helps each motor follow its target rather than fight the linkage.

Tune the response visually: set the sensor's neutral reference, then drag curve points or enter values to choose how sensed roll and pitch move the wings. Three presets let different responses be compared.

Wing angles first, motor angles second: roll gives a mirrored left/right response, while pitch acts on both wings. The curves combine into 0–70° wing commands, and the linkage calculation converts each command into two motor targets.

Keep motion separate from the dashboard: one ESP32 handles sensing and tuning; the other controls the motors. Manual wing and individual-motor modes help check the mechanism before trying automatic operation.

Test the physical result: position feedback corrects tracking errors, and lost encoder data or communication disarms the motors. The sensor estimates tilt from acceleration, so response under braking, cornering, and aerodynamic load still needs testing.

specs.label: Actuation
specs.value: 4 DC motors with magnetic position feedback

bom.detail: Two ESP32 DevKit boards: N1 for motor control, N2 for sensing and the dashboard
MPU6050 accelerometer and gyroscope module; current wing commands use accelerometer-derived roll and pitch
Four MT6701 magnetic encoders, one per motor
Four DC motors through H-bridges; motor and driver models are not specified in the code
125 mm and 100 mm arms, 55 mm motor-shaft spacing, and a 30 mm wing-carrying connecting link per side

projects.title: Tekkai 2.0
projects.subtitle: An autonomous sumo robot with three ultrasonic sensors, two edge sensors, remote motor enable, and an onboard Wi-Fi debug interface.
projects.summary: An autonomous sumo platform with three ultrasonic sensors, two edge sensors, remote motor enable, and an onboard Wi-Fi debug interface.
notes: The current firmware adds two active-low edge inputs and remote ON/OFF control, alongside the three ultrasonic opponent sensors.
Edge readings are confirmed over multiple samples. A timed reverse-and-search response handles simultaneous front-edge detection; other branches combine target direction and edge state.
The debug page exposes sensor readings, speed, motor state, and a motor test. The linked 2024 repository below is an earlier implementation and does not contain all 2026 behavior.

projects.title: CupExS Drag Racer
projects.subtitle: A Wi-Fi-controlled drag car, a separate two-lane infrared finish timer, and a companion motor-dyno experiment.
projects.summary: A Wi-Fi-controlled drag car, a separate two-lane infrared finish timer, and a companion motor-dyno experiment.
notes: The current car controller provides browser Start / Stop commands, 20 kHz 10-bit forward PWM, and an automatic stop after a 60-second run window.

A separate ESP32 timer alternates 36 kHz bursts across two lanes, handles a countdown, and records independent finish times when beams are interrupted. The browser control does not synchronize the vehicle launch to the timer.

The companion dyno firmware samples an MT6701 encoder and ACS712 current sensor and estimates torque and power from a configured inertia. It is a separate test program; its current GPIO21 reverse-drive / encoder-SDA overlap must be reconciled with the wiring.
CAD and fitted motion models in the workspace support drivetrain experiments. No competition placing or certified power result is inferred from the photographs.

projects.title: Door Security System
projects.subtitle: An ESP32 door monitor combines an infrared beam, motion-based tamper detection, a buzzer, a local web panel, and optional email alerts.
projects.summary: An ESP32 door monitor combines an infrared beam, motion-based tamper detection, a buzzer, a local web panel, and optional email alerts.
notes: The controller emits NEC-coded IR at 38 kHz and watches receiver CH1. A confirmed beam interruption while armed latches the alarm.
MPU6050 tilt, angular speed, and acceleration changes are checked against a calibrated baseline, with a confirmation interval to reject brief disturbances.
The web panel switches Open / Armed modes and shows a bounded breach log. Wi-Fi credentials and Gmail app credentials are supplied locally; no private configuration is included in the repository.

projects.title: GYM Scale
projects.subtitle: A BLE-connected ESP32 load-cell scale with filtered weight telemetry and a Flutter companion app for local measurements and food logging.
projects.summary: A BLE-connected ESP32 load-cell scale with filtered weight telemetry and a Flutter companion app for local measurements and food logging.
notes: HX711 readings pass through a median window and a Kalman-style denoiser after startup tare. The configured calibration factor and 10 kg capacity must match the actual load cell.
A versioned 16-byte BLE packet carries readiness flags, sequence, uptime, grams, and raw delta. Notifications are limited to a 200 ms interval.

The Flutter app scans and subscribes over BLE, checks packet validity and stale readings, and uses local SQLite storage for food and measurement workflows. This is a prototype platform, not a certified weighing instrument.
